subject: Converting Relative Risk to Predicted Probabilities

messages.author: 5c834f66d44ea056
messages.subject: Converting Relative Risk to Predicted Probabilities
parts:
Hello INLA experts,

I am using INLA package in which my dependent variable is observed cases of a disease like this

formula <- Y ~ f(id, model = "besag", graph = g, scale.model = TRUE) + f(id1, model = "iid")

where Y is the observed cases

res <- inla(formula, family = "poisson", data = data_map, E = Expected, control.predictor = list(compute = TRUE) )
In the above Expected is the expected number of cases.

Now I am aware that res$summary.fitted.values$mean   will produce Relative Risk for all my IDs but I want to ask how I can produce predicted probabilities for all my IDs . Does the res object produce it ? or Do I need to make some change in the parameters for INLA above.

Thanks!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Converting Relative Risk to Predicted Probabilities
parts:
The fitted values for the Poisson

y ~ Poisson(E * exp(eta))

will be

fitted.values = exp(eta)

note that 'E' is NOT included.

like this:

> r=inla(y ~ 1, data=data.frame(y=200,E=2), E=E, family="poisson", control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))
> r$summary.fitted.values$mean
[1] 100.247275

while

> r=inla(y ~ 1, data=data.frame(y=200), family="poisson", control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))
> r$summary.fitted.values$mean
[1] 200.4945483



if you want ``probabilities'' there is no unique way to get those. usually, but not always, then if

y ~ Poisson(E * exp(eta))

this is a shorthand, or an approximation, for

y ~ Binomial(size=N, prob=p)

so you can define

E * eta = N * p

*if* you know what 'N' is
